# jwe — spec

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E2 A2 H1 P3 · limited by scope (core), performance (not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** core — go-jose v4.1.5 / panva jose (JWE compact) (surveyed 2026-09-30)

**Audit:** review 2026-09-03 · mutation 2026-11-21 (172/178, 6 eq) · src 59f481e58c37917b

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-10-10 (200,000-run budget per harness clean, JWE_FUZZ) · ct 2026-11-13 (ctgrind, decrypt side, tainted key per kind: dir CEK 18, AxxxKW/GCMKW KEK 5, ECDH-ES static key 8, PBES2 password 3, RSA-OAEP key 20 in-file, unattributed 0; every context is a designed public verdict, itemised under Constant-time; the encrypt side draws its secrets internally and emits only public ciphertext, so it takes no tainted input) · panic 2026-11-13 (sweep of every pub entry point: an `apu`/`apv`/`iv`/`tag`/`p2s`/`epk` member over 128 bytes overran the header encoder's base64 scratch, now `HeaderTooLarge`/`BufferTooSmall`; the Concat KDF accepts an empty output and panics with a checked message beyond its 32-bit fields; a GCM plaintext past 2^36 - 32 bytes is `BufferTooSmall`)

**Performance:** not measured

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

**Where we are ahead:** the only Zig JWE known; RFC 7516 Appendix A worked examples as tests;
verify-before-decrypt CBC-HMAC with a single error for tag or padding failure; refuses `zip`
outright (a deliberate anti-zip-bomb stance that go-jose, which implements DEF, does not take)
and caps PBES2 iterations (`default_max_p2c`). **Where we are behind:** JSON
serialization and multiple recipients (deliberate for v1, see *Design*), RSA1_5 (refused, see *What is deliberately not done*), ECDH-ES on P-384/P-521 (→ Backlog).

Design + threat notes for auditors. Usage: see ./README.md.
Attribution/provenance: see ./NOTICE (module-local — see its own note on
placement).

## Design & invariants

- **Layout:** `header.zig` (JOSE Protected Header build/parse, pure
  `std.json` + `std.base64.url_safe_no_pad`, no crypto) → `enc.zig` (content
  encryption, RFC 7518 §5) and `alg.zig` (key management, RFC 7518 §4), both
  dispatched from `root.zig`'s `encryptCompact`/`decryptCompact`. `enc.zig`'s
  `cbc_hmac` builds on the shared `aescbc` module (raw AES-CBC + PKCS#7
  padding — see `modules/aescbc/SPEC.md`) for its CBC half; `alg.zig`'s
  AxxxKW/PBES2-* paths wrap/unwrap through the shared `aeskw` module (RFC
  3394 AES Key Wrap — see `modules/aeskw/SPEC.md`). Both were extracted FROM
  this module's own original implementations, so their KATs and error
  shapes are unchanged. `kat_rfc7516.zig` carries the two RFC 7516 Appendix A
  full-token worked examples as tests.
- **Compact serialization only** (RFC 7516 §3.1). The General/Flattened JSON
  serializations (§7.2) are explicitly out of scope for v1: they exist to
  carry **multiple recipients** (one `encrypted_key` per recipient, one
  shared `ciphertext`/`tag`) sharing one CEK — this module's
  `KeyMaterial`/`encryptCompact` shape is single-recipient by construction
  (one `alg` + one key in, one `encrypted_key` out). Adding JSON
  serialization later means adding a multi-recipient encrypt entry point,
  not just a different framing — a real API change, not a formatting detail.
- **`gpa`-owned results, not caller-supplied fixed buffers.** Unlike `rsa`
  (bounded by a fixed max modulus) or `jwt` (bounded token/claim sizes via an
  arena), JWE plaintext is arbitrary application data with no natural upper
  bound. `encryptCompact`/`decryptCompact` allocate their result from the
  caller's `gpa` (mirroring `jwt`'s arena-owned `ParsedToken`); every
  internally-bounded value (CEK, encrypted key, IV, tag, header JSON) still
  uses fixed-size stack scratch — the zero-alloc rule applies wherever a size
  genuinely is bounded.
- **AAD = the raw header segment bytes**, never a re-encoding. Both
  `encryptCompact` (which builds the header once and reuses those exact
  base64 bytes for both the wire segment and the AAD) and `decryptCompact`
  (which uses the token's original header substring directly, never
  re-serializing the parsed JSON) avoid any JSON-canonicalization mismatch
  between "the header as written" and "the header the tag was computed
  over" — a classic JOSE interop footgun sidestepped by construction.
- **AES-192 comes from sibling modules, not std.** std's `crypto.core.aes` ships only `Aes128`/`Aes256`
  and `crypto.aead.aes_gcm` no `Aes192Gcm` (checked against Zig 0.17.1's std); all GCM sizes run on
  `aesgcm`. `A192CBC-HS384`'s CBC half runs on `aes192.Aes192` through `aescbc`; `A192GCM` and
  `A192GCMKW` on `aesgcm.Aes192Gcm`; `A192KW`, `PBES2-HS384+A192KW` and `ECDH-ES+A192KW` through
  `aeskw`'s 24-byte KEK arm. 128/256 stay on std. Anchors: RFC 7518 B.2 byte-exact both directions,
  McGrew–Viega 10 (A192GCM) and 8 (as a GCMKW wrap), RFC 3394 §4.2/§4.4 in `aeskw`, and a full-token
  round trip of every A192 `alg` × `enc` pair (RFC 7520 has no AES-192 example).
- **Direct modes carry no Encrypted Key.** RFC 7516 §5.2 step 10 requires the segment to be empty for
  Direct Encryption (`dir`) and Direct Key Agreement (`ECDH-ES`); `decryptCompact` returns
  `error.MalformedToken` for bytes in it. The segment is outside the AAD, so without the check anyone
  could splice bytes into it and the token would still decrypt, a second, different token for the same
  message.
- **Every algorithm is implemented and KAT-validated.** The KATs are listed under *Verification*;
  `aeskw` and `aescbc` were extracted from this module's own implementations, so their KATs and error
  shapes are unchanged. RFC 7516 A.3 (`A128KW` + `A128CBC-HS256`) is asserted byte-exact in both
  directions (decrypt, the raw key wrap against §A.3.3, encrypt against §A.3.7 with the RFC's CEK and
  IV fed through a fixed byte stream); A.1 (RSA-OAEP) in the decrypt direction only, OAEP being
  randomized.

## Threat model

- **Key-material confusion** (the JWE analogue of `jwt`'s RFC 8725
  algorithm-confusion defense): `KeyMaterial` is a tagged union of six arms
  (`symmetric`/`rsa_public`/`rsa_private`/`password`/`ec_public`/`ec_private`), and both
  `encryptCompact` and `decryptCompact` check the header's `alg` against the
  *kind* of key material supplied before doing any crypto —
  `error.KeyMaterialMismatch` on any mismatch (an `RSA-OAEP` token can never
  be "verified" against a symmetric key, etc.).
- **`zip`-bomb rejection:** `header.parse` refuses any header carrying a
  `zip` member outright (`error.UnsupportedZip`), encode or decode. This
  module implements no decompression; "decrypt attacker-controlled
  ciphertext, then decompress the result" is precisely the shape of a
  compression/zip-bomb amplification attack (and the general class CRIME/
  BREACH belong to, whenever compression crosses a trust boundary) — refusing
  it outright is cheaper and safer than trying to bound it.
- **RSA-OAEP randomness:** `encryptOaep`'s security proof requires an
  unpredictable seed; `rsaOaepWrap`'s entropy parameter is never optional.
  Because OAEP is randomized, `KAT` round-trip testing of the RFC 7516 A.1
  vector can only assert the DECRYPT direction — see `kat_rfc7516.zig`.
- **The randomness seam is a named union, not a `std.Random`.**
  `encryptCompact`, `alg.rsaOaepWrap` and `ecdhes.generateEphemeral` take
  `Entropy` (`entropy.zig`), whose two arms are `.csprng` (the caller's claim,
  unverifiable here — `std.Random` is a vtable) and `.fixed_for_test`. The
  weak path still exists; it can no longer be reached without writing its
  name, which is the bar this repo's RNG-seam audit sets. Consequence, stated
  per mode because it is not uniform: under `dir` the CEK *is* the caller's
  long-lived key, so a repeated content IV under `A128GCM`/`A256GCM` recovers
  plaintext (`C1 XOR C2 = P1 XOR P2` — GCM is CTR underneath, so the leak is
  full-length, not a prefix) **and** exposes the GHASH subkey `H = E_K(0^128)`
  from the two tags, giving forgery of every other token under that key; under
  `AxxxCBC-HSxxx` a repeated IV leaks only plaintext-block-prefix equality and
  recovers no key; under every non-`dir` `alg` the CEK is drawn fresh per call,
  so the damage is confined to the messages that shared the draw.
  **Why not fail-closed** (module draws its own entropy via `io: std.Io`, as
  `bfv`/`tfhe` do): this module is a pure codec with no I/O authority, and the
  injection point is load-bearing for its strongest external anchor — RFC 7516
  §A.3 is reproduced byte-exact **in the encrypt direction** by feeding the
  RFC's published CEK ‖ IV through a fixed byte stream (`kat_rfc7516.zig`).
  **Why not merely documented:** documentation changes what a careful reader
  knows, not what a careless one can express.
  **Why not structurally prevented:** `encryptCompact` is a pure function over
  caller-owned key material; guaranteeing IV uniqueness needs per-key state
  surviving process restarts, and the deterministic alternative (SIV, RFC
  5297) is not an RFC 7518 §5 `enc` value, so it would not be JWE.
- **Header-size-bounded decode:** `decryptCompact` rejects a base64url
  header segment longer than `header.max_header_b64_len` (16 KiB) before
  doing any base64/JSON work — bounds the allocation a decrypt call performs
  on fully attacker-controlled input (the header segment) before any crypto
  or authentication has run.
- **Fail-closed authentication:** GCM tag mismatches return
  `error.AuthenticationFailed` and never write partial/garbage plaintext to
  the caller-visible result (std's `aead.decrypt` itself does not write on
  failure). The CBC-HMAC core (`enc.zig`) verifies the tag via
  `std.crypto.timing_safe.eql` BEFORE running any CBC decryption (a
  Vaudenay-style padding oracle is exactly what verify-after-decrypt, or a
  non-constant-time compare, reopens), and its PKCS#7 padding validation is
  branch-free over the final block with any failure surfacing as the SAME
  `error.AuthenticationFailed` as a tag mismatch — a padding error is
  indistinguishable from an authentication error to the caller.
- **The `AL` (AAD length) encoding footgun** (RFC 7518 §5.1 step 5 / §5.2.2.1
  step 4): `AL` is the **bit** length of the AAD, as an **8-byte big-endian**
  integer — not the byte length, not little-endian, not the ciphertext's
  length. Getting this wrong produces a tag that "looks like" it should
  verify and doesn't (or, on crafted inputs, a genuine forgery surface).
  Handled in `cbc_hmac.computeTag` and pinned by the RFC 7518 Appendix B
  KATs (which carry the expected `AL` bytes verbatim).
- **Const-time AES-KW integrity check** (`aeskw.unwrap`): the final
  comparison of the recovered register against `default_iv` goes through
  `std.crypto.timing_safe.eql` — an early-exit compare would turn a
  wrong-KEK/corrupted-input unwrap into a timing oracle. On failure the
  output buffer is zeroed (`std.crypto.secureZero`) so no partially-unwrapped
  key material leaks to the caller.
- **Out of scope for v1:** General/Flattened JSON serialization (multiple
  recipients — see Design above), and any `enc`/`alg` this file doesn't
  list. `ECDH-ES` / `ECDH-ES+A128KW` / `ECDH-ES+A256KW` (RFC 7518 §4.6,
  elliptic-curve key agreement on P-256 or X25519 + the Concat KDF) ARE in
  scope and implemented — see `ecdhes.zig`, byte-exact against RFC 7518
  Appendix C. `ECDH-ES+A192KW` included (its KEK goes to `aeskw`'s AES-192
  arm).

## Constant-time (ctgrind)

`src/ctgrind_harness.zig`, driven by `scripts/checks/ctgrind.sh jwe`; the pinned table is in
`scripts/checks/ctgrind-expected.tsv` (ReleaseFast, unattributed 0, controls and traps 0).
Decrypt only: a token is built with an untainted key copy, the decryptor gets a tainted copy,
accept and a flipped-octet reject per algorithm. The plaintext length is public once the tag
verified: the harness's own copy / print / free use the length of the plaintext it sent, checked
against the returned (declassified) one; the module's own branches on it stay counted. On baseline
x86-64 (`scripts/test.sh ctgrind-portable`) the counts are `cpu=x86_64` variant rows: std's soft-AES
key schedule (A1) and its `undefined` batch padding (A2) add contexts, none a jwe branch on a key.

- **content 18** — GCM tag verdict `aesgcm` root.zig x3 (one per key size); CBC-HMAC tag
  verdict `enc.zig` x6 (`timing_safe.eql` result, accept + reject, 3 encs), checked BEFORE any
  decryption; PKCS#7 unpad result `aescbc` root.zig x2; the plaintext length
  (`root.zig` `n == plaintext.len` x3, its realloc std Allocator.zig / PageAllocator.zig x4).
  All public: accept/reject, and a length the authenticated sender chose.
- **kw 5** — `aeskw` root.zig unwrap integrity verdict x2, `aesgcm` :1048 x3 (content tag + GCMKW
  unwrap tag at `alg.zig`/`:116`). The unwrap verdict only picks the §11.5 decoy CEK.
- **ecdh 8** — `ecdhes.zig` `rejectNonCanonical(d)` x2 (true for every valid key), p256
  `group.zig` identity-result verdict x1 (delegated), std `curve25519.zig` `x2.isZero()`
  identity verdict x1, `aeskw` :171 x2, `aesgcm` :1048 x2.
- **pbes2 3** — `aeskw` :171 x2, `aesgcm` :1048 x1; PBKDF2 over the tainted password raises none.
- **rsa 20** (10 per `RSA-OAEP` / `RSA-OAEP-256`) — `rsa` root.zig F3 fault-check verdict;
  root.zig the OAEP decode's single decision point (`valid != 1`); root.zig the recovered
  message copy, whose size-class branches in the std memcpy are 6 contexts; `jwe` root.zig
  `got.len != cek_len`; `aesgcm` :1048 content tag. The OAEP decode itself is branch-free
  (leading byte, lHash compare, separator scan and padding check are folded into one flag, no
  early exit by failure reason), so Manger's oracle has nothing to read. A bad key unwrap, of any
  kind, substitutes a decoy CEK (RFC 7516 §11.5) and runs the same content decryption, ending in
  the same `AuthenticationFailed` as a bad tag; a ciphertext that decodes validly with a correct
  length is one whose sender (anyone, the key is public) knew the CEK, so it opens no oracle.

## Verification

Run: `scripts/modtest jwe`. Tests sit beside the code (`src/root.zig`, `enc.zig`, `alg.zig`,
`ecdhes.zig`, `header.zig`, `kat_rfc7516.zig`, `sweep_test.zig`, the two stack probes).

- **Content encryption** (`enc.zig`): `A128GCM`/`A256GCM` real round trips and tamper detection;
  `A192GCM` against McGrew–Viega test case 10; RFC 7518 B.1/B.2/B.3 (`A128CBC-HS256`, `A192CBC-HS384`,
  `A256CBC-HS512`) byte-exact `E` and `T`, both directions; the CBC-HMAC fail-closed test (a tag
  mismatch and a padding failure are the same error); a non-block-aligned plaintext; a std-only
  sanity oracle for B.1; a content tag one octet too long is refused, not truncated.
- **Key management** (`alg.zig`, `root.zig`): `dir` (CEK is the shared key, wrong length refused, a
  non-empty Encrypted Key refused); RSA-OAEP-256 round trip on RFC 7516 A.1's 2048-bit key; GCMKW
  for all three sizes (A256: every KEK byte load-bearing; A192: McGrew–Viega case 8 as a wrap);
  PBES2 wiring, the `max_p2c` and `p2s >= 8` edges, and the RFC 7517 Appendix C.4/C.5 KAT; AES-KW
  through `alg.aeskw` (RFC 3394 §4.1); wrapped CEKs and GCMKW `iv`/`tag` of the wrong length are
  `InvalidKey`; a failed unwrap never decrypts under a predictable CEK (the RFC 7516 §11.5 decoy), and
  every Encrypted Key failure is one error value.
- **ECDH-ES** (`ecdhes.zig`, `root.zig`): the RFC 7518 Appendix C KATs (P-256 `Z` and the Concat-KDF
  derived key, byte-exact); a std oracle for the Concat KDF and its counter loop; round trips for
  `ECDH-ES`, `+A128KW`, `+A256KW` (X25519), `+A192KW`; cross-curve and key-material confusion are
  typed errors; off-curve, bad-length, zero/non-canonical-scalar and low-order peers are refused;
  `PrivateKey.wipe` zeroes the scalar.
- **End to end:** every A192 `alg` × `enc` pair round-trips; RFC 7516 A.1 (decrypt) and A.3 (both
  directions) full-token KATs in `kat_rfc7516.zig`; key-material confusion (a `dir` token against an
  RSA key), unknown `alg`/`enc`, an empty header segment, `expect_alg`/`expect_enc`, header and member
  size limits at max + 1, non-empty `aad_extra`, `zip` and `crit` refused, an attacker-chosen PBES2
  work factor refused, not performed.
- **The entropy seam:** `Entropy` has exactly two arms, and a test shows the CSPRNG requirement is
  load-bearing (`dir` + `A256GCM` with a repeated generator reuses the IV).
- **No-panic sweep** (`src/sweep_test.zig`, one test per finding): an over-long byte member is
  `HeaderTooLarge`/`BufferTooSmall`, an empty Concat KDF output derives nothing, a GCM plaintext past
  2^36 − 32 bytes is an error, a header nested thousands of levels deep is refused, junk segments of
  odd lengths never crash under any `alg` and `enc`.
- **Dead-stack residue:** two `STACKPROBE` tests (ReleaseFast/ReleaseSmall only) look for key, scalar
  and `Z` residue after ephemeral generation, `deriveZ`, the KDF, `encryptCompact`/`decryptCompact` under
  ECDH-ES, and `pbes2DeriveKek`.
- **Fuzz:** harnesses generic over their choice source, run by `std.testing.fuzz` and by the
  deterministic driver `JWE_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]` (testkit's fuzz driver): `decryptCompact` on
  arbitrary tokens, an encrypt + decrypt round trip (a genuine JWE opens, a flipped one is refused), and
  `header.parse` on arbitrary header JSON. Reach tests fail unless every outcome is hit; corpus tests
  pin how far each seed gets, and a TEETH test checks that the decrypt harness reaches the header
  parser.
- **Constant time:** the ctgrind harness (`src/ctgrind_harness.zig`) and its pinned table, see
  *Constant-time (ctgrind)*.
- **Mutation.** A whole-module strict schemata run over `header.zig`, `root.zig`, `alg.zig`, `enc.zig` and `ecdhes.zig`: 178 mutants on the header parse (member type, base64url length and alphabet, `p2c` range, member caps at `max_member_len`, `zip`/`crit`) and encode caps, the `p2c` bound and `p2s` minimum, the RFC 7516 section 11.5 collapse (each error class kept apart) and the decoy CEK, the `alg`/`enc` dispatch (RSA-OAEP hash, PBES2 variant and PRF, KEK sizes, AlgorithmID, entropy draws), the empty-Encrypted-Key rules, every length check of the GCM and CBC-HMAC primitives and their tag compares, the ECDH-ES curve and coordinate checks and the Concat KDF. 172 are killed and 6 equivalent. 64 survived the first pass and are now killed by tests: the CEK, wrap IV and PBES2 salt coming from the entropy in order, RSA-OAEP and RSA-OAEP-256 and all three PBES2 variants end to end, the decoy being keyed (a token sealed under the key-less hash of its Encrypted Key does not open), a missing `p2s` or `p2c` refused, the ECDH-ES typed errors, PBES2-HS384/HS512 key derivation against an independent PBKDF2 oracle, exact length edges of every primitive, and a P-256 `epk` without `y` where `(x, x)` is a curve point. Equivalent: `encryptCompact`'s unknown-`enc` check (the next line returns the same error), the CBC-HMAC empty-ciphertext check (unpadding refuses it with the same error), `OutOfMemory` kept out of the collapse (`unwrapCek` never allocates), and three decoy details only a holder of the key can observe (domain string, binding to the Encrypted Key, the tail beyond the digest of a 64-octet CEK). Not mutated: the point arithmetic (owned by `p256`) and the dead-stack burns.
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over the last whole-module
  mutation run and the delta runs after it.

## What is deliberately not done

- **RSA1_5** (RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5) — not offered, following `rsa`'s "What is deliberately not done". A JWE
  producer can always choose RSA-OAEP, unlike the SAML IdPs that force `xmlenc` into `rsa-1_5`, and
  RFC 8725 §3.2 advises against RSA1_5. Revisited only if a consumer's peer cannot be changed; it would
  then be off by default and with implicit rejection, as in `xmlenc`.
- **`zip` (DEFLATE) compression** — refused outright (`UnsupportedZip`), see *Threat model*; go-jose
  implements it, this module takes the anti-zip-bomb stance.

## Anchoring

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

- **Class A** — wire/interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it.
- **Oracle EXTERNAL** — published vectors, goldens captured from a foreign implementation, or a test run against a live foreign peer.

**What the tests actually contain.** RFC 7516 App A full-token KAT (kat_rfc7516.zig) + RFC 7518 App B/C KATs

## Backlog / deferred

- **ECDH-ES on P-384 / P-521** — `ecdhes.Curve` is `p256`/`x25519` only; go-jose and panva/jose accept the
  NIST curves and IdPs commonly publish P-384 keys. Effort: medium (needs a P-384 primitive;
  `std.crypto.ecc.P384` is the likely base *(inferred, not checked)*). Fits §2: yes.
- **JWE JSON serialization (flattened/general) and multiple recipients** — go-jose and panva/jose both
  ship it; deliberately out of scope for v1 (see *Design & invariants*), listed because it is an API
  addition, not a framing change. Effort: medium. Fits §2: yes.
- **Performance not measured** — the AES-GCM bulk path runs in `aesgcm` (see its Performance); jwe has no
  bench of its own.
